locations.description: Arco de la Estrella and Plaza Santa María (Season 7, Episode 3) Situated in the middle of the Plaza Mayor, atop a wide flight of stairs between Moorish towers, is the Arco de la Estrella, which was and still is the main entrance to the ‘Ciudad Monumental’, a maze of narrow cobbled streets, stone houses and centuries old residences of monarchs and noble families.  Nowadays, most of these buildings are museums or local government offices. In Game of Thrones, however, this is all part of King’s Landing and makes a fitting backdrop to the scene in which Euron Greyjoy arrives on horseback, dragging his rope-bound prisoners through the streets which are filled with crowds of abusive hecklers.  Among those prisoners are Yara Greyjoy, Ellaria Sand and her daughter, all of whom are forced to endure the insults of the mobs whilst being pelted with random objects as Euron, on the other hand, receives a hero’s welcome. This public parading of the prisoners begins in the Plaza Santa María and ends at the Arco de la Estrella before Euron enters the palace of Cersie Lannister, which was recorded elsewhere.
locations.name: King's Landing

locations.description: Bhaktapur Durbar Square, situated in Bhaktapur, Nepal, is an ancient royal palace complex. It served as the residence of the Malla kings from the 14th to the 15th century and later as the home of the kings of the Kingdom of Bhaktapur from the 15th century until the late 18th century, when the kingdom was conquered in 1769.
locations.name: Bhaktapur Durbar Square

locations.description: Kirtipur is an ancient city and municipality in Nepal. The Newars, indigenous to Kipoo, call it home. Situated 5 km southwest of Kathmandu, Kirtipur lies within the Kathmandu Valley and is one of its five densely populated municipalities, along with Kathmandu, Lalitpur, Bhaktapur, and Madhyapur Thimi.
locations.name: Kritipur

locations.description: The Bagmati River flows through Nepal's Kathmandu Valley, acting as a natural boundary between the cities of Kathmandu and Patan. It then continues through Madesh Province in southern Nepal, eventually merging with the Kamla River in Bihar, India. This river holds religious significance for both Hindus and Buddhists, with numerous Hindu temples situated along its banks.
locations.name: Bank of Bagmati, Pashupatinath

locations.description: Boudhha, named for its massive stupa, serves as a pilgrimage site for Tibetans. Devotees walk around the shining white dome, which is decorated with painted Buddha eyes, and visit nearby monasteries and schools for prayers and seminars.
locations.name: Boudha, Kathmandu

locations.description: Rinpung Dzong, also known as Paro Dzong, is a significant dzong (Buddhist monastery and fortress) of the Drukpa Lineage of the Kagyu school in Bhutan's Paro District. It accommodates the district's Monastic Body and the government administrative offices of Paro Dzongkhag. The dzong is also listed on Bhutan's Tentative List for UNESCO World Heritage inclusion.
locations.name: Rinpung Dzong

locations.description: Swayambhunath is an ancient religious complex located atop a hill in the Kathmandu Valley, west of Kathmandu city. The site's Tibetan name, "Sublime Trees", refers to the diverse varieties of trees found on the hill.
locations.name: Swayambhunath

locations.description: Kathmandu Durbar Square is a historically and culturally important site in Kathmandu, Nepal. It is one of the three Durbar (royal palace) Squares in the Kathmandu Valley that are recognized as UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
